sources.citation: Fabre, Alain. 2005-. Diccionario etnolingüístico y guía bibliográfica de los pueblos indígenas sudamericanos, entry JENIPAPO-KANINDÉ (last modified 2009-10-09), 1 p.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States: 'Lengua sin clasificar y extinta. El grupo étnico habla solamente portugués.' Notes Loukotka (1968: 91) lists genipapo and kanindé as extinct and assigns them 'sin proporcionar pruebas' to the Tarairiú stock; whole bibliography is ethnographic/historical.

sources.citation: Girão, Valdelice Carneiro. 1991. Os índios Paiacu: primeiros habitantes de Pacajus. Revista do Instituto do Ceará (ano 1991, tomo 105), 8 pp.
sources.note: No phonology content. Opening sentence: 'Os Baiacu, Paiacu ou Pacaju, apesar do nome tupi, eram tribos indígenas de língua travada, classificados pelos primeiros cronistas como nação tapuia'; notes Pompeu Sobrinho affiliated them to the Tarairiú; rest is colonial history from Théberge, Studart, Studart Filho. No words.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian Languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center, p. 91 (Tarairiú stock).
sources.note: Nothing. Under the Tarairiú stock: 'Canindé - once spoken at the sources of the Chorro River, state of Ceará.' and 'Genipapo - Portuguese name of an extinct language on the Chorro River.' No source, no words; the only Tarairiú data are three words (agh 'sun', kén 'stone', ake 'tobacco').

sources.note: Nothing; Tarairiú 'attested only through a few word lists' (three words from Loukotka); Jenipapo-Kanindé appears only as an ethnic division of the Tarairiú nation.

sources.citation: Studart Filho, Carlos. 1965. Os aborígenes do Ceará (Coleção História e Cultura, dirigida pelo Instituto do Ceará). Fortaleza: Editora Instituto do Ceará. sources.note: No phonology content. The only linguistic characterisation is that the Baiacu/Paiacu were 'gentios de lingua travada a quem os primeiros cronistas chamavam Tapuia' (non-Tupi speech); classification is by ethnohistorical inference; not a single word of Payaku/Canindé/Jenipapo speech is cited anywhere in the book (a full-text search for stress/accent the full djvu text for vocabulário/idioma/dialeto confirms only Kariri and Tupi material).

sources.citation: Pompeu Sobrinho, Thomaz. 1964. Onomástica indígena cearense. Revista do Instituto do Ceará (ano 1964, tomo 78), 23 pp.
sources.note: No phonology content relevant to this languoid; Tupi-based etymologies of Ceará place names only.

sources.citation: Studart Filho, Carlos. 1962-1963. Os aborígenes do Ceará [I-II]. Revista do Instituto do Ceará (anos 1962 e 1963; c. 4 MB scanned PDFs each in the archive.org RIC mirror).
sources.note: Nothing. Both instalments downloaded tonight through ia_fetch.sh and read (a full-text search for stress/accent the full text for acento/tônica/oxítona/prosódia/fonética/pronúncia/tom/sílaba/vocabulário/língua/dialeto plus all Jenipapo/Canindé/Paiacu passages). Part I (RIC 76, 1962) is physical anthropology, material culture and a classification that lists Canindés, Paiacus/Baiacus, Jenipapos and Jenipapoaçus among the Tarairiú; its only phonetic remark (note 35, p. 70-71: meanings 'dependendo apenas do tom com que se pronuncia o vocábulo') concerns the Tupi word Abaeté, not Jenipapo-Kanindé.…

sources.citation: Pompeu Sobrinho, Thomaz. 1958. Línguas tapuias desconhecidas do Nordeste: alguns vocabulários inéditos. Boletim de Antropologia (Fortaleza) 2(1): 3-19.

sources.citation: Studart Filho, Carlos. 1958. Notas históricas sôbre os Baiacu do Ceará. Revista do Instituto do Ceará 72: 15-34.
sources.note: No phonology content; 20 pages of colonial history (1666-1818). No words of the language.
